strengths: Hikaru Nakamura exhibits exceptional performance with the White pieces, particularly in aggressive and less common openings. He has a remarkable 91% win rate in 46 games facing the Nimzo-Larsen Attack, and a perfect 100% win rate in 26 games facing the Nimzowitsch-Larsen. His success in these lines suggests a deep understanding and comfort with non-mainstream approaches.

As Black, Hikaru Nakamura demonstrates a highly reliable repertoire, notably employing the Modern Defense in 114 games with an impressive 87% win rate. He also achieves a 100% win rate in 13 games playing the Indian Defense and 13 games playing the Neo-Old Indian / Modern, showcasing versatility and strength in various setups.

Across analyzed positions, Hikaru Nakamura generally maintains strong tactical accuracy, with an average of 0.42 mistakes per game. This indicates a low propensity for blunders and a solid calculation ability.
weaknesses: Hikaru Nakamura shows a notable vulnerability when facing the Queen's Gambit Accepted as Black, with a win rate of only 33% in 9 games. This suggests opponents might find success by entering this specific opening variation against him.

When playing White, Hikaru Nakamura has struggled against the Ruy Lopez, Anderssen Variation, achieving only a 29% win rate in 7 games. This specific variation appeared in 7 games and appears to pose challenges for his White repertoire.

Instead, focus on building slow, strategic advantages and creating subtle positional pressure. However, his slightly elevated mistake rate in specific lines like the Queen's Indian Accelerated (1.00 mistakes per game, appearing in 3 games) suggests that if an opponent can steer the game into less familiar or extremely sharp territory for him, tactical opportunities might arise. Exploit any early inaccuracies aggressively, as he typically converts advantages efficiently.
